newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel faces 19 bln DM shortfall, Kohl backs him -- MPs.
newsitem.headline: Waigel faces 19 bln DM shortfall, Kohl backs him -- MPs.

text.p: Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Tuesday he was 19 billion marks short in his 1997 budget and Chancellor Helmut Kohl backed him up in plans for spending cuts and more privatisations, deputies at a meeting said.

Waigel told deputies in a closed-door meeting he expected to take in 10 billion marks from sales of Bonn's shares in Deutsche Telekom and another three billion from cuts in planned spending, the deputies said.
Waigel also said he could not rule out tax increases, an option Kohl's Free Democrat (FDP) coalition partners vehemently oppose.
The minister said Bonn could also increase revenues by selling some of its holdings in Lufthansa, the Postbank, highway petrol concessions and other properties, they said.

The deputies said Kohl said he shared responsibility for the current situation and threw his suport solidly behind Waigel, saying he would rebuff all criticism of him during a parliamentary debate on the budget on Thursday. He urged them to close ranks behind Waigel.
